A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RadZero and VL-CABS, with matching core methods, experiments, and figures. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite v3's expanded supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, grounding, phrase-grounding, segmentation, and ablation results, including Tables 1–10 and qualitative visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds computational measurements, classification evaluations, linguistic similarity analyses, and five-seed experimental results.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, finding-sentence extraction, VL-CABS computation, MP-NCE/InfoNCE objectives, and zero-shot inference procedures are unchanged. Alternative encoders are experimental ablations; Appendix F's suggested normalization of abbreviations does not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: The clinical training and benchmark coverage remains unchanged. Appendix F adds text-similarity retrieval scenarios testing syntactic variation, related vocabulary, and rare or unseen abbreviations. The alternative CheXpert split changes protocol rather than clinical coverage; CT and MRI remain future directions.

E2.justification: New Table 15 compares RadZero against published supervised results for ConVIRT, REFERS, M3AE, MGCA, and MRM. M3AE and MGCA appeared in different comparisons in v2, but their classification comparison is new. Table 7 also replaces the M3AE encoder condition with DINOv2; the main zero-shot comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds several evaluation protocols: a different CheXpert test split for supervised comparisons, H100 resource benchmarking with batch-one latency and maximum-fitting-batch throughput, and sentence-neighbor retrieval tests. Table 7 replaces M3AE at 224 pixels with DINOv2 at 518 pixels. These are added or revised experimental settings, while the main benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds linguistic robustness and abbreviation-failure analyses in Appendix F, a resolution–cost trade-off study in C.2, and a classwise investigation of ChestXray14 underperformance in D.1. The encoder ablation is revised, while the existing view-position, trainable-layer, text-encoder, batch-size, and visualization analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v2 provides point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty summaries. v3 Appendix G explicitly reports additional experiments across five random seeds and supplies means and standard deviations for the main tasks in Table 18. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although no comparative significance tests or confidence intervals are provided.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, but v3 adds resource measurements, per-finding AUCs, supervised comparisons, retrieval similarities, and repeated-run summaries. Table 18 reports CXD10 grounding at 0.601 ± 0.013 alongside the retained 0.622 point estimate. Table 15's new CheXpert score of 0.889 uses a different split; Table 7 replaces M3AE results with DINOv2 results under different encoder and resolution conditions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, normalization, attention computation, losses, and inference equations retain their substance. Replacing transpose-product notation with inner-product brackets is equivalent notation. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the advertised application from radiology to chest X-ray in the title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The central contributions and claims concerning VL-CABS, explainability, multi-positive learning, and zero-shot multi-task capability remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning encoder domain mismatch, dataset-dependent emphysema performance, computational trade-offs, linguistic generalization, and run-to-run stability. It explicitly limits validation to chest X-rays and identifies weak alignment for rare abbreviations. These extend the earlier limitations concerning generalization, encoder dependence, and imperfect localization.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a RadZero code-access link and detailed memory, latency, throughput, and measurement configurations. Reported training time changes from 16 to 13 hours on four H100 GPUs. Section 4.3 newly identifies the test set as the Dice-threshold tuning set; v2 left that unspecified. These disclosures do not establish a changed training schedule or threshold-selection procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for BioBERT, REFERS, and MRM and expands comparison with supervised radiograph-learning methods. The main related-work discussion and positioning relative to LiT, dino.txt, UniCLIP, CARZero, and other medical VLMs remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. v3 makes localized language corrections, revises the conclusion, updates author order and conference information, regroups the appendices, and adds funding acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. The added scientific material does not involve wholesale rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the tabular presentation with computational, per-finding, supervised-comparison, linguistic-similarity, and uncertainty tables. It reformats Figure 7's extraction prompt across the page width, expands and splits the abbreviation table, and rearranges appendix tables. The existing ten figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important evidential gap by adding five-seed variability reporting for central results in Table 18. New classwise and computational analyses expose failure patterns and practical trade-offs, while explicit chest-X-ray scope, threshold-tuning disclosure, and code-access information improve transparency. The linguistic evidence remains qualitative, and mean/standard-deviation reporting does not establish comparative statistical significance, but the additions substantially strengthen assessment of the paper's reliability and applicability.
